{{Only primary sources|date=May 2025}}
In mathematics, a '''nilcurve''' is a pointed [[stable curve]] over a [[finite field]] with an [[indigenous bundle]] whose [[p-curvature|''p''-curvature]] is square nilpotent. Nilcurves were introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Shinichi Mochizuki|last=Mochizuki|year=1996}} as a central concept in his theory of [[p-adic Teichmüller theory]].

The nilcurves form a stack over the [[moduli stack]] of stable genus ''g'' curves with ''r'' marked points in characteristic ''p'', of degree 
''p''<sup>3''g''–3+''r''</sup>.
